# download_audio_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Download new videos from a genre's configured channels as MP3 and back them up to a locker.

## Synopsis

```
download_audio_files [options]
```

## Description

Takes no URL. The channels come from `story_channels` and `asmr_channels` in
`Shared/joybox/config/audio.py`, and only the `Story` and `ASMR` genres download
anything; the other genres are accepted but do nothing. For each channel:

1. Lists the channel's videos with `yt-dlp --flat-playlist` (Rumble channels are
   scraped directly) and drops those already in the channel's download archive,
   `Audio/Archive/<genre>/<channel>.txt` under the file metadata directory.
2. Downloads the rest in batches of `audio_download_batch_size` (25) with yt-dlp,
   extracting MP3 with the thumbnail and metadata embedded, named
   `<upload date> - <title>.mp3` and then sanitized.
3. After each batch, copies the audio to `Music/<genre>/<channel>` in each locker
   selected by `-l`, skipping files already there, and removes the working copies.

Each batch works in a temporary directory unless `-o` is given. With `-o` each channel
works in `<output_path>/<channel>`, which is kept, and the next run first uploads any
audio an interrupted run left there. yt-dlp also resumes partly downloaded videos.

Download order follows `audio_download_oldest_first` in the same config file (newest
first by default); `--oldest_first` and `--newest_first` override it for one run.
Each video is fetched with `audio_download_concurrent_fragments` (4) parallel
fragments, capped at 8, with a 3-5 second pause between videos.

## Options

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-g, --genre_type <genre_type>` | Genre whose channels to download; only `Story` and `ASMR` do anything. Allowed: `ASMR`, `Audiobook`, `Classical`, `Game`, `Radio`, `Regular`, `Soundtrack`, `Story`, `Therapy`. |
| `-c, --cookie_source <cookie_source>` | Browser to read cookies from (passed to yt-dlp as `--cookies-from-browser`), or the path of a cookies file (passed as `--cookies`). Default: `firefox`. |
| `-n, --channel_name <channel_name>` | Download only channels whose configured name matches, case-insensitively: an exact match if there is one, otherwise every name containing it. No match stops the run and lists the names. |
| `--oldest_first` | Download each channel's new videos oldest first, overriding `audio_download_oldest_first`. |
| `--newest_first` | Download each channel's new videos newest first, overriding `audio_download_oldest_first`; wins if both order flags are given. |

### Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-l, --locker_type <locker_type>` | Locker to copy the audio to; `All` means every configured locker. Default: `All`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Directory to keep each channel's downloads in (`<output_path>/<channel>`) so an interrupted run can resume; a temporary directory per batch when omitted. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Download new videos from every Story channel

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story
```

### Download one channel (case-insensitive, substrings allowed)

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -n "Mr Nightmare"
```

### Fill in a channel's back catalogue oldest first

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -n "Mr Nightmare" --oldest_first
```

### Download ASMR and back it up to the local locker only

```bash
download_audio_files -g ASMR -l Local
```

### Use Chrome's cookies

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -c chrome
```

### Use a cookies file

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -c /path/to/cookies.txt
```

### Keep downloads in a folder so an interrupted run can resume

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -o ~/audio_resume
```

### Stage a large backlog in the local locker only, to push later with master_backup

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -o ~/audio_resume -l Local
```

### Show each channel's archive file and target folder without downloading

```bash
download_audio_files -g Story -p -v
```

## Notes

- Re-runs only fetch videos not in the download archive, so the tool is safe to run repeatedly.
- YouTube needs the Deno JavaScript runtime to solve its download challenge; without it downloads fail with `Requested format is not available`. Deno is looked for at `~/.deno/bin/deno` and on `PATH`.
- If a channel's videos cannot be listed, the whole channel URL is handed to yt-dlp in one pass.
- A yt-dlp exit code of 1 counts as success, since it is also what yt-dlp returns when some videos fail or everything was already archived; members-only videos fail this way unless the cookies belong to a member. Higher exit codes stop the run.
- Copies to remote lockers happen file by file and print nothing without `-v`. For a large backlog, use `-l Local` and then `master_backup`, which uploads in batches.
- Under `-p` no yt-dlp command is run: channels are not listed and nothing is downloaded, but the log still shows each channel's archive file and target folder.
